active.title: c5: .dadaiaignore replaces instance_exceptions.txt, a two-level root canon, init scaffolds the root files, core protected in two layers
active.description: Operator design (grill 2026-09-26, ADRs 0092-0096), back in 0.5.0 by ADR 0101 (operator 2026-09-29). Deliver: a root .dadaiaignore, operator-only and PROTECTED, replacing .dadaia/states/instance_exceptions.txt 1:1 (0092); its stdlib grammar, invalid line = doctor finding (0093); level-1 library core in core/workspace_layout.py incl. worktrees/ and .dadaiaignore, level 2 = .dadaiaignore (0094); init creates prompt.md, AGENTS.md, .dadaiaignore from a template (0095); gate blocks agent writes to core law/state, doctor --fix at SessionStart self-heals missing core, no Bash parsing (0096). Today: root whitelist exists; worktrees/ and .dadaiaignore absent from canon. Blocks canonical-worktrees (worktrees/ must be canon) and operator-protected-path-class. OPEN QUESTIONS for the operator (not resolved by the product engineer): (1) grill R2 'a missing .venv is fixed by uvx dadaia-workspace init <ws>' vs ADR 0067 (without the venv every gate wrapper warns and exits 0) and open bug missing-venv-hook-disarms-the-gate-invisibly: without the venv core protection's gate layer is off - which rules? (2) ADR 0092 / grill Q6 applies .dadaiaignore to harness directories, but ADR 0059 (later) says the doctor judges only ledger-owned entries there - does .dadaiaignore reach harness-dir interiors or only their top level? (3) ADR 0096 'no Bash parsing' vs the idea gate-judges-bash-writes (closure ruling 2026-09-28) - keep both, or reject one?

active.title: DEC-11: an operator-protected path class the gate enforces in every harness
active.description: Deferred by ADR 0053 (2026-09-27) and kept deferred by ADR 0101 (operator 2026-09-29) until the operator rules otherwise. Today an operator-only folder inside a consumer repo is guarded only by one harness's permissions.deny; Codex and the others carry no protection. Remediation-plan DEC-11 options: (a) an operator glob file read by the gate in every harness (about +25 lines), the law stating Bash is not covered (backstop git/pre-push); (b) keep it per-harness config plus the git backstop, the law saying so. Recommendation (a). Grill 2026-09-26 Q2 routed 'operator-declared protection file' to the backlog. Depends on dadaiaignore-and-root-core-canon (same operator-file grammar). Open question: (a) or (b), and whether it is a second operator file or a section of .dadaiaignore.
